steps.u: The daily cold-chain temperature report says some reefer containers had 2x the readings they should. Find out where the duplicates come from and fix the pipeline step.

12 def clean(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
13     df = df.dropna(subset=["temp_c"])
14     df["ts"] = pd.to_datetime(df["ts"], utc=True)
15     df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=["device_id", "ts"])
16     return df[(df.temp_c > -40) & (df.temp_c < 30)]

steps.a: The duplicates are the same reading (same device and sequence number) delivered twice by the gateway, which retransmits under at-least-once delivery, and on the retry the gateway stamps its own receive time, so ts differs by a few hundred milliseconds and dedup on (device_id, ts) misses them. I could round ts to the second, but that would still miss retries that cross a second boundary (RF-02003 above) and could merge genuinely distinct readings; the device sequence number is the reading's identity, so I'll dedup on (device_id, seq) and keep the earliest ts.

steps.a: Cause: gateway retransmissions under at-least-once delivery, re-stamped with a slightly later receive time, so dedup on (device_id, ts) didn't catch them. The cleaning step now dedups on (device_id, seq), keeping the earliest timestamp. On the 18 Nov file that removes 108,436 duplicate rows; no device now exceeds 1,440 readings a day (one per minute). Added a test for a retry that crosses a second boundary; all 6 tests pass.

reference.summary: Found that duplicated cold-chain sensor readings came from gateway retransmissions under at-least-once delivery that were re-stamped with a later receive time, so deduplicating on device and timestamp missed them. The pandas cleaning step now deduplicates on device and sequence number keeping the earliest timestamp, removing about 108k duplicates from one day's file, with a new test passing.
facts: Duplicates had the same device and sequence number but timestamps a few hundred milliseconds to over a second apart
